A Router now answers 404 for a path that none of its routes match, where it answered a confusing 502, `sst remove` stops blanking the generated type files, projects in a directory with `.sst` in its name build again, and Next.js segment prefetch requests get their own CloudFront cache entry. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

Thanks to [@AliAladraj](https://github.com/AliAladraj), whose two fixes are carried here, and to [@bchilcott](https://github.com/bchilcott), [@rwilsonjones](https://github.com/rwilsonjones), [@alyyousuf7](https://github.com/alyyousuf7) and [@bevdam](https://github.com/bevdam), who reported the problems behind four of the changes.

### Fixes

- **A Router answers 404 for a request that matches none of its routes, instead of a 502.** It applies to a Router created with `routes` and no `/*` route, which now answers with a 404 page, and to a Router whose routes are added with `router.route()` or `router.routeBucket()`, which answers with a plain `404 Not Found`. Before, those requests were sent to the Router's placeholder origin and came back as a 502. To catch the other requests, add a route for `/` (a `/*` route in `routes`), and the docs for `route()` and `routeBucket()` now say so. A request still passes through as before when no routes are registered yet, when the list of routes can't be read, and when a route matches but its data can't be read. A list of routes stored in chunks that failed to read halfway used to fail the function with a 503, and it no longer does. ([#202](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/202), by [@AliAladraj](https://github.com/AliAladraj); [#200](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/200), reported by [@rwilsonjones](https://github.com/rwilsonjones); [#204](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/204); [#203](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/203))
- **`sst remove` no longer blanks the generated type files.** Removing a whole stage, or its last component, keeps the types in `sst-env.d.ts` and `sst.pyi` from the last `sst deploy` or `sst dev`, so removing one stage no longer breaks type checking for another. A remove that leaves links still updates the types from what remains, as does a `--target` remove. ([#201](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/201), by [@AliAladraj](https://github.com/AliAladraj); [#199](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/199), reported by [@bchilcott](https://github.com/bchilcott))
- **Projects whose path contains `.sst` build again.** A directory such as `app.sst-branch`, for instance a git worktree of a branch that starts with `sst`, made `sst.config.ts` fail with `ReferenceError: sst is not defined`, because the `sst` and provider globals were not injected anywhere. They are injected into every file now except the ones inside the project's own `.sst` directory, which includes a project opened through a symlink. ([#206](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/206); [#205](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/205), reported by [@alyyousuf7](https://github.com/alyyousuf7))
- **Next.js segment prefetch requests no longer reuse the full page's CloudFront cache entry.** The Router includes the `next-router-segment-prefetch` header in the cache key, so a request for a route's segments and a request for the full page are cached separately. Requests without the header keep the cache key they had, so existing cache entries stay valid. ([#208](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/208); [#207](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/207), reported by [@bevdam](https://github.com/bevdam))

### Also

- The Router's route lookup uses shorter local names, because the merged changes had left less than the 2,000 bytes of the function's 10,240 that the room for a user's injection needs. The lookup does the same as before ([#210](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/210); [#209](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/209)).

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.23.1
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.23.1"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
